title: Enbridge franchise agreement and gifts rules for councillors
subtitle: Code of Conduct gift exception, Integrity Commissioner report, Elliott board appointments and a martial arts champion honoured.
overview: Council asked the Province to let municipalities charge gas utilities for using public land, and directed staff to negotiate a new franchise agreement with Enbridge Gas on that basis. Council also gave in-principle support to a provincial bill on the issue. Several youth and climate delegates urged support, while Enbridge said the model agreement is set across Ontario and costs would likely reach local ratepayers anyway.

Council also amended the Code of Conduct to exempt food, lodging, transportation and entertainment provided by third parties for events aimed at a municipal government audience. Benefits over $300 must be reported within 30 days. This followed the Integrity Commissioner's report finding the Mayor had breached the existing gifts rules inadvertently, with no penalty recommended. An amendment requiring prior council approval was defeated {{vote:m6}}. Councillors noted that a governance review in March will include the Code of Conduct.

After a closed session, council appointed two people to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees. It also heard that it received information and gave staff direction on bargaining for two CUPE locals; no further details were reported. The Mayor presented a city medal to a local martial arts world champion.

decisions.detail: Council amended Section 5 of the Code of Conduct to allow third-party-provided food, lodging, transportation and entertainment at municipal-audience events, with reporting within 30 days when the benefit exceeds $300 {{vote:m7}}.
Council defeated an amendment that would have required council approval for benefits over $300 and approved an exception for the Mayor's Global Covenant of Mayors work {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Request to Province on gas utility fees
decisions.detail: Council asked the Province to amend Regulation 584/06 so municipalities can charge for-profit gas utilities fees for using public property {{vote:m10}}.

Staff were directed to negotiate a franchise agreement allowing fees if the regulation changes, avoiding city liability for gas relocation costs and keeping future charges off Guelph customers {{vote:m11}}.
Council supported in principle the "No Free Ride for Fossil Fuels Act, 2024" tabled by the local MPP {{vote:m12}}.
Council will send the Enbridge motions and a letter of support for Bill 219 to provincial officials, Ontario Big City Mayors, AMO and member municipalities {{vote:m13}}.
Council appointed Joanne Hohenadel and Lisa Woolley to the board for a three-year term ending November 26, 2027 {{vote:m2}}.

debate: On the gifts amendment, the mover said the original wording was too broad because anyone could accept benefits and report afterward. Prior approval would add transparency.

Opponents said the amendment would be cumbersome, could politicize routine decisions and create many agenda items, and should not be drafted on the fly. Several favoured addressing the gap in the March governance review instead.
Delegates for youth and climate groups called free use of public land a hidden subsidy to a fossil fuel company, and linked it to environmental budget cuts and rising emissions.

Enbridge said it pays property taxes, has funded relocations in Guelph without city contributions, and follows a province-wide model agreement. It said the Ontario Energy Board would likely let franchise fees be passed to ratepayers.

One councillor opposed the franchise clauses because fees would likely be passed to ratepayers and add to energy poverty. Another said the clauses are aspirational and that fee revenue could fund retrofits and support for low-income households.
